title: Reliability activation lab: weekly probes and ownership radar
content:
Context and intent:
This doc defines the first 8-week Reliability Activation Lab: a lightweight, cross-functional program to operationalize SLOs for prioritized model-serving services and to exercise escalation/runbook flows before a larger SLO rollout. The lab is intentionally experimental — weekly probes, short retros, and a visible ownership radar to catch handoff gaps early.

Why now:
- Several product teams are preparing service-level commitments for Dedicated customers.
- Observability coverage for model-serving latency and tail-errors is incomplete for new routing paths (edge + regional fallback).
- We want to validate that error-budget driven runbooks and canary rollback loops operate end-to-end with oncall, platform, and product stakeholders.

Objectives (clear, measurable):
1) Instrumentation coverage: achieve 90% telemetry coverage for latency (P50/P95/P99), QPS, error-category breakdown, and request path tag propagation for the two pilot services by week 3.
2) SLO sanity check: Define service SLOs and acceptance gates (availability and latency) and run two controlled budget burn experiments with <10% customer impact by week 6.
3) Runbook maturity: Publish executable runbooks for the top 3 failure modes with playbooks verified by SRE and service owners by week 5.
4) Handoff clarity: Ownership radar (matrix) shows clear primary/secondary owners for infra, runtime, monitoring, and product decisions for all pilot routes by week 2.

Scope and pilots:
- Pilot services: model-router-v2 (chat endpoints) and embedding-ingestor (batch embedding pipeline).
- Excluded: on-prem private deployments (will be a future lab).

Success criteria (for lab completion):
- >90% of alerts have a documented runbook linked from PagerDuty alerts.
- Two planned experiments completed: one latency spike simulation (traffic shaping), one error-injection (non-production path) with documented outcomes.
- Rollout template for SLO gating (canary thresholds, rollback triggers) accepted by product and platform leads.

Weekly cadence and artifacts:
- Weekly probe sessions (1.5h) — Thu 10:00–11:30: short experiment + immediate 15-min retro; notes posted to Confluence.
- Ownership radar update — Tues sync (15m) to adjust owners and blockers.
- Weekly summary email to stakeholders with burn metrics, runbook changes, and decision log.

Playbook of probes (examples):
Week 1: Baseline capture — collect 14-day telemetry, sample traces, and map current alert-to-runbook links.
Week 2: Ownership radar finalize + instrumentation gap sprint (obs tickets).
Week 3: Canary traffic shift (10% -> 25%) to exercise latency SLOs and route fallback.
Week 4: Controlled error injection in staging to simulate KV cache corruption; verify cache warmup and fallback behavior.
Week 5: Runbook table-top with oncall (walkthrough of top-3 incidents) and update runbooks.
Week 6: Budget burn experiment 1 (latency microburst, <5% traffic affected).
Week 7: Post-mortem simulation — inject staggered regional failures in staging, validate multi-region fallback and RTO.
Week 8: Consolidation, SLO gating template adoption, and handoff checklist to program teams.

Measurements and observability requirements:
- Metric set: request_count, success_rate(by error_category), latency_ms(P50/P95/P99), kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_depth.
- Trace sampling: ensure traces include model_id, route_version, origin_region tags.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO dashboard with error budget burn chart (7d & 30d), latency histogram, and rollback count.
- Alert rules: two classes — P0 (pagable) and P1 (ticket); attach runbook IDs to alert definitions.

Experiment safety and customer impact controls:
- All active experiments run first in staging and perf-cluster; production probes start at <1% traffic and require sign-off from service owner + SRE lead.
- Circuit breaker: automated traffic-shift abort if P95 latency > 2x baseline for >5m or error_rate spike > 3x baseline for >2m.
- Observability rollback timeline: teams must be able to revert traffic shift within 5 minutes.

Runbooks and responsibilities (ownership radar snapshot):
- Primary SRE oncall (runbook steward): Asha Patel — maintain runbook and verify PagerDuty links.
- Platform infra (scaling & routing): Liam Chen — traffic shift tooling and autoscale tuning.
- Service owner (code & deploy): Priya Malhotra — approve canaries and rollback.
- Monitoring & telemetry: Diego Alvarez — ensure metrics tags and dashboards reflect experiment fields.
- Product impacts and customer comms: Rosa Kim — owns stakeholder notification and external comms template.

Decision gates and rollout criteria:
- Instrumentation gate (week 3): must have 90% of top-1000 request traces tagged with model_id and route_version.
- Canary gate: if during a 25% canary shift, error budget burn rate exceeds 1.5x expected, abort and investigate.
- Runbook gate: every P0 alert must have a documented owner and escalation path before broader SLO adoption.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: missing observability for edge fallback paths. Mitigation: short spike on ingress path and distributed tracing verification in week 1–2.
- Risk: coordination friction between product and infra during mid-experiment rollbacks. Mitigation: pre-authorized rollback roles and a 5-min decision SLA for experiments.
- Risk: experiments trigger third-party rate limits. Mitigation: vendor throttling simulation and vendor contact on standby.

Communication and stakeholder list:
- Weekly digest to: eng-leads, platform, product-safety, customer-success.
- Slack channel: #sre-activation-lab (use for experiment play-by-play).
- Confluence page: Reliability Activation Lab (living document).

Oncall and escalation protocol (short):
1) PagerDuty alert fires -> runbook steps executed by primary oncall.
2) If not resolved in 15m -> escalate to service owner and platform lead.
3) If error budget burn projected to exhaust within 24h -> open an incident and run escalation (exec notify template in Confluence).

Decision log (initial entries):
- 2026-08-18: Kickoff approved by SRE manager (Evelyn Park). Scope: model-router-v2 and embedding-ingestor.
- 2026-08-25: Instrumentation sprint assigned (Liam and Diego) after baseline review.
- 2026-08-31: Canary template defined; threshold P95 120ms for chat endpoints agreed as preliminary SLO.

Open questions to resolve in next 48h:
- Confirm exact PagerDuty alert IDs to attach runbooks to (ask Asha for mapping).
- Finalize the low-risk production traffic-shift tool (feature flagging vs router-level split).
- Decide retention window for trace sampling for pilot (14d vs 30d).

Next immediate actions (owners):
- Evelyn: publish this doc to Confluence and schedule weekly probe sessions.
- Liam: create instrumentation tickets for route tagging (due 2026-08-24).
- Diego: deploy updated dashboards to staging (due 2026-08-26).
- Priya: nominate secondary service owner for embedding-ingestor (due 2026-08-24).

Appendix: useful links and quick references:
- SLO design primer (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Design+Primer
- Canary tooling repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-runner
- PagerDuty runbook mapping guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/PagerDuty+Runbooks

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working document; expect frequent updates after probe sessions. Please add comments inline on Confluence, and flag any blockers by assigning to the owner in Slack.
